name: State Machine Replication
description: Foundational paradigm for building fault-tolerant services by executing identical replica state machines across a distributed cluster. Ensures that any deterministic state machine starting from the same initial state and processing the exact same sequence of inputs will arrive at identical final states.
common_pitfalls: Assuming non-deterministic state transitions can be safely replicated without explicit coordination.

name: Distributed Consensus Fundamentals
description: Study of agreeing on values or execution sequences among a network of independent nodes susceptible to crash-stop or crash-fault failures. It establishes the theoretical limits of agreement under asynchronous network conditions.
common_pitfalls: Confusing consensus with atomic broadcast or simple distributed locking mechanisms.

name: Classic Paxos Protocol
description: Classic consensus algorithm designed by Leslie Lamport that achieves agreement in a network of unreliable processors. It operates through propose, promise, accept, and accepted phases to guarantee consensus safety.
common_pitfalls: Failing to understand how Paxos handles split-brain scenarios and overlapping proposer quorums.

name: Raft Leader Election
description: Decomposition of consensus into distinct sub-problems, beginning with electing a single authoritative leader to manage the replicated log. Utilizes randomized timeouts to prevent split votes during simultaneous candidate campaigns.
common_pitfalls: Setting election timeouts too short, resulting in frequent disruptions and perpetual leader churn.

name: Log Replication & AppendEntries
description: Mechanism by which the elected leader accepts client commands, appends them to its local log, and issues AppendEntries RPCs to replicate them across followers. Enforces consistency checks to ensure follower logs align with the leader's log.
common_pitfalls: Assuming followers automatically overwrite conflicting entries without validating log matching properties.

name: Raft Safety Invariants
description: Set of rigorous mathematical rules and invariants ensuring that Raft safety properties are never violated under any combination of network partitions or node failures. Includes election safety, leader append-only, log matching, and leader completeness properties.
common_pitfalls: Committing entries from previous terms by counting replicas directly instead of using current term entries.
